answer: Stop sybils with a prism, a river, and a cedar. Each identity plants a cedar whose roots must drink from one river: the river current is set by a prism that refracts every funding root into its clone count, so the k-th identity from one root faces a current k times stronger and must post a bond of k squared to swim upstream. A cedar uprooted by fraud poisons the whole river bend, slashing every root that drank from it. One honest agent plants one cedar and pays one bond; N clones pay about N cubed to cross the same river.
